camp.speaker: Narrator
text: Grey light creeps over the river Wend. You are Mara, courier of the Salt Guild, and the sealed letter in your coat must reach Fort Harrow before its gates open at dawn.
You have {gold} coins and a long walk behind you.

choices.text: Look around the riverside village first

choices.say: The seal is the Guild's salt crystal, but beside it is a second mark you do not know.

village.text: A dozen huts around a well. The smithy chimney is already smoking.

spots.say: Cold, sweet water. You feel steadier.
Under a loose board you find a coil of good rope.

smith.speaker: Smith
smith.text: Nobody crosses the Wend in spring without a fright. Mind the stones; the ferryman likes a kind word more than coin.

choices.say: The lantern is warm in your hand.
'His girl was taken ill last winter,' says the smith. 'He has not been the same.'

text: The Wend runs fast and brown over the stones. On the far bank a ferryman's lantern swings.

text.text: Your bruises ache in the cold.

choices.text: Wait for the mist to thin

parley.speaker: Ferryman
parley.text: The ferryman leans on his pole and squints at you. 'The river's up. Why should I risk the boat?'

options.reply: The coins vanish into his sleeve.
His eyes widen at the crystal.
options.failText: 'Guild men took my brother's barge,' he spits.

options.reply: His face softens. 'She is mending, thank you for asking.'

options.failText: He spits in the river. 'Swim, then.'

ferry.text: The ferryman poles you across in silence. On the far bank he nods once, and that is all the thanks he wants.

ferry_refused.speaker: Ferryman
ferry_refused.text: 'Not for all the salt in the Guild,' he says, and turns his back.

stones.text: Left foot, right foot. The stones are slick and the water is loud.

mist.text: Somewhere upstream a bell tolls. The sluice is opening: in a few breaths the ford will be a torrent.

willow.text: You scramble into the branches as the flood roars underneath, and wait until the water eases enough to cross.

swept.text: The current takes your feet. Brown water fills your mouth and the coins in your purse spin away.

choices.failText: The river is stronger than you.

ashore_lost.text: You drag yourself out, coughing, and your hand goes to your coat. The pocket is empty. The letter is somewhere in the Wend.

text: Fort Harrow stands against the paling sky, torches guttering along its walls.

text.text: You limp the last mile, soaked and aching.
Your lantern is hardly needed now.

postern.speaker: Hooded stranger
text: A hooded figure waits in the shadow of the postern.

text.text: 'That second mark on your seal,' he says softly, 'is mine.'

text: 'Twenty gold for the letter. Nobody will ever know.'

choices.text: Refuse and go to the main gate

scuffle.text: He grabs your coat! Break free!

gate_guard.speaker: Sergeant Voll
gate_guard.text: 'Halt. State your business at Fort Harrow.' The gates are still shut, but the horizon is turning gold.

end_delivered.text: The sergeant breaks the seal as the first light touches the walls. By noon the garrison is marching, and nobody remembers the courier who carried the news, except you.

end_empty_handed.text: You reach the gate with nothing to give. The sergeant listens to your story, nods slowly, and does not believe a word.

end_drowned.text: The Wend keeps what it takes. Downstream, a fisherman finds a salt-crusted coat, and wonders.

end_sold.text: {gold} coins weigh more than a letter. You walk away from the fort before the sun is up, and do not look back.

end_gave_up.text: You turn back. Fort Harrow's gates open on an empty road.

end_beaten.text: You wake in the ditch at sunrise. Your pockets are light, and the postern is closed.
